elements.element: The renewal mechanism must use one of the permitted preferred models: renewal only by mutual written agreement, or automatic renewal subject to the preferred automatic-renewal protections.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the permitted automatic-renewal model for both the Agreement and the Attachment.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal period must be twelve (12) months.
elements.evidence: Both the Agreement and the Attachment automatically renew for periods of twelve (12) months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to prevent renewal on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: For both the Agreement and the Attachment, IBM may give 30 days' written notice of its intent to terminate, within the operative automatic-renewal sentence.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a renewal reminder at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence requires MSL to notify IBM in writing not less than 60 days before the end of the then-current term of the upcoming renewal.

elements.element: Any renewal-period price increase must not exceed the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that any price increase for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: The fallback may use automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: Both the Agreement and the Attachment renew automatically.

elements.element: Customer's non-renewal notice requirement must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: IBM's notice requirement is 30 days for both the Agreement and the Attachment, which is below the 60-day maximum.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The operative cap is the lesser of CPI and 3%, and therefore does not permit an increase above 5%.

result.reason: The redline implements the preferred automatic-renewal alternative across both instruments: 12-month renewal periods, 30-day Customer notice, a Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and the required price cap. The changes are confined to renewal mechanics and preserve the initial terms and existing termination references. Drafting quality is reduced because the reminder phrase “before the end of the then-current term of the upcoming renewal” is awkward, and “intent to terminate” is less precise than an express notice of non-renewal.
